# Signal-to-Proof

Title: Signal-to-Proof — Evidence-Gated Correlation & Causality Modeling
Author: Gerry Sun / GRDigital
Website: https://www.geraldrobert.com/
Repository role: Public technical demonstrator

## Summary
Signal-to-Proof is a decision-oriented measurement system that separates correlation, controlled association, quasi-experimental inference, and randomized causal evidence. It validates data and identification conditions before assigning an evidence grade, then emits an allowed claim, blocked claim, limitation, and next evidence step.

## Core files
README.md — executive and technical overview
ARCHITECTURE.md — system architecture
METHODOLOGY.md — statistical and causal methodology
EVIDENCE_LADDER.md — evidence grades and claim ceilings
DECISION_SYSTEM.md — strategy, economics, product, UX, GTM, data, ML, and causal integration
EVALUATION_GUIDE.md — recommended review path
IP_BOUNDARY.md — public/private implementation boundary
REFERENCES.md — public methodological references
src/signal_to_proof/ — executable reference implementation
tests/ — claim-boundary and failure-mode tests
docs/index.html — static visual walkthrough

## Important interpretation rules
- Correlation is not causality.
- Controlled observational models do not create a counterfactual.
- Outcome depth and causal strength are separate dimensions.
- Prediction can guide what to test but does not establish intervention effect.
- A causal claim requires a defensible counterfactual and a design capable of identifying the effect.
- The public implementation is intentionally bounded and does not expose private production methods.
